examples.en: Select a menu item on the screen.
For the language, choose Korean.

examples.ko: 어느 방을 선택했어요? — 바다가 보이는 방을 선택했어요.
examples.en: Which room did you choose? — I chose the room with a sea view.
Salary matters too when you choose a job.

examples.ko: 두 가지 중에서 한 가지만 선택해요.
examples.en: You choose only one of the two.

explain: 말할 때는 ‘고르다’를 더 많이 써요. ‘선택하다’는 화면, 시험, 서류처럼 조금 격식 있는 곳에서 많이 나와요.

dict_examples.ko: 글을 쓸 때에는 목적에 맞는 글감을 잘 선택하고, 이를 효과적으로 표현하는 것이 중요하다.

explain_en: In everyday speech people use 고르다 (pick) more. 선택하다 is a bit more formal and shows up on screens, tests and forms.

examples.en: Read the first sentence.
Repeat the next sentence after me.
The exam has a sentence-writing question.

examples.en: I memorize one new sentence every day.

examples.ko: 문장이 너무 길어요. 짧게 써 주세요.
examples.en: The sentence is too long. Please write it shorter.

explain: 문장은 하나의 끝난 말이에요. 문장이 여러 개 모이면 ‘글’이 돼요. 말할 때는 ‘말’, 쓸 때는 ‘문장’을 많이 써요.

explain_en: A 문장 is one complete sentence. Several sentences together make a 글 (a piece of writing). People say 말 for speech and 문장 mostly for writing.

examples.en: Write your answer here.
My friend isn't answering my message.
One answer on the test was wrong.

examples.ko: 이 문제의 답은 뭐예요? — 삼 번이에요.
examples.en: What's the answer to this question? — It's number three.
If you don't know the answer, ask a friend.

explain: 메시지나 이메일에 답하는 것은 ‘답장’이라고 해요: 답장을 보내다. 말로 대답하는 것은 ‘대답’이에요.

dict_examples.en: The answer is correct.

explain_en: Replying to a message or email is called 답장: 답장을 보내다. A spoken reply is 대답.

examples.en: Put your pens on the desk.
Put the keys on the dining table.
I put the vase in the middle of the table.

examples.ko: 그 컵은 싱크대 옆에 놓아 주세요.
examples.en: Please put that cup next to the sink.

examples.ko: 저는 가방을 의자에 놓고 손을 씻었어요.
examples.en: I put my bag on the chair and washed my hands.

explain: 다른 동사 뒤에 ‘-아/어 놓다’를 붙이면 ‘그 상태로 해 두다’라는 뜻이에요: 문을 열어 놓다, 미리 사 놓다.

explain_en: Add -아/어 놓다 after another verb and it means “do it and leave it that way”: 문을 열어 놓다 (leave the door open), 미리 사 놓다 (buy ahead).

examples.en: I left my umbrella in the classroom.
I left my phone at home.
I keep milk in the fridge.

examples.ko: 카페에 우산을 두고 와서 다시 갔어요.
examples.en: I left my umbrella at the café, so I went back.
Leave your bags here and look around.

explain: 놓다는 ‘내려놓는 동작’이고, 두다는 ‘그 자리에 계속 있게 하는 것’이에요. 그래서 물건을 잊고 왔을 때는 “두고 왔어요”라고 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: to take something to heart, to dwell on

My textbook isn't in my bag.
We get our textbooks at school at the start of a new term.
This textbook has a lot of pictures.
I bought one Korean textbook.

explain: 교과서는 학교 수업에서 쓰는 책이에요. 학원이나 개인 수업의 책은 보통 ‘교재’라고 해요. 시험 문제만 있는 책은 ‘문제집’이에요.

It's raining. Open your umbrella.
We spread out a mat in the park and sat down.
Open your fist.
I lay out my bedding every evening.

explain_en: 펴다 means to open out something that is folded or bent. Its opposite is 접다. It is used for books, umbrellas, bedding, hands and your back.

I folded the clothes and put them in the wardrobe.
The rain stopped, so I folded my umbrella.
The child folds an airplane out of paper.
I fold the laundry. My younger sibling helps me.

Please erase the board.
I erase wrong answers with an eraser.
I deleted a lot of photos from my phone.
I deleted my friend's number by mistake.

en: write down what you hear; take dictation

examples.en: Write down this sentence as you hear it.
Write down what the teacher says.
I listen to the news once and write it down.
I wrote down the address my friend read out to me.
Write down the important things in your notebook.

explain: ‘받아쓰기’는 들은 말을 쓰는 연습이에요. 한국 초등학교에서 많이 해요. 한국어 맞춤법 공부에 아주 좋아요.

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 받아쓰기 is dictation practice: writing down what you hear. It is common in Korean primary schools, and it is great practice for Korean spelling.

examples.en: Your writing is too big. Please write a little smaller.
If I write fast, my handwriting isn't pretty.

explain: ‘글씨’는 손으로 쓴 글자 모양을 말해요. 인쇄된 글자나 컴퓨터 글자는 보통 ‘글자’라고 해요.
